findings.title: beads-closed-gate swallows a refused br read into an empty --beads scope — the open-bead audit silently drops the wave and the gate green-lights
findings.evidence: `_scoped_raw=$(br_call show --json $BEADS_SCOPE) || _scoped_raw=""` converts ANY br_call refusal (rc 2: dead board read, error envelope, bad id in the list) into an empty string; the jq guard then turns it into SCOPED_BEADS="[]" and SCOPED_COUNT=0. When CLAIMED_COUNT>0 the FAIL-CLOSED at line 401 does not fire, so FULL_SCOPE (line 420) collapses to FULL_CLAIMED alone and the OPEN-bead check (line 423) audits only claimed beads — an open in-wave bead held by NO assignee, the case lines 417-419 explicitly claim still blocks, silently drops out of the audited population and line 453 passes. The gate's own comment (396-399: 'a --beads list that resolves to nothing still leaves SCOPED_COUNT at 0 and still exits 2') is true only when the assignee also has zero claims. This is the one conversion site in the thirteen-site wave that maps a refused read to empty data; every other site (close-gate, coordinator, flight-check, board-truth, stamp-refined, diff-closure, needs-device-gate, close-evidence-check, claim-race-harness, refly, element4-check) exits NOT-GATED/CANNOT-CHECK on the same refusal. Attack path: actor = conductor running the close gate; entry = one transiently dead br read (or one unresolvable id in --beads, which — per br-contract C5's envelope-on-stdout behaviour — refuses the whole show); gain = a 'safe to close' verdict for a batch whose open --beads beads were never examined.
findings.fix: Make the refusal refuse, matching the wave's other twelve sites: `_scoped_raw=$(br_call show --json $BEADS_SCOPE) || { echo "beads-closed-gate: FAIL-CLOSED — the br show read for --beads refused; the batch scope cannot be resolved (never an empty one)" >&2; exit 2; }`. Keep the existing type=="array" guard for legitimately partial resolutions only.

findings.title: Check 36's raw-read regex misses two formatting evasion classes — a future raw br --json read ships uncaught
findings.evidence: RAW_READ matches per-line. Probed live against the shipped regex: (1) a raw read split on a line continuation (`br show \` + `  --json "$1"`) matches on NEITHER line — line 1 lacks `--json`, line 2 lacks `br`; (2) a quoted binary literal (`"br" show --json`) does not match because `\bbr\b` requires whitespace immediately after `br` and the `"?\$\{?BR\}?` alternative requires `$`. Both produce a tree on which 36-br-envelope.py exits 0 (verified with the file during this review: neither line trips RAW_READ) while containing the exact dead-read-as-empty-data defect the check exists to make a red commit. The D9 population is defined by invocation SHAPE; these are the same invocation with different whitespace, the classic evasion class for a line-oriented classifier (cf. the registry's own doctrine: unit-test the evasion CLASS — line-break/whitespace splits). The check's test fixture covers none of these (36-br-envelope.test.sh has zero continuation/quote cases). Attack path: actor = any agent authoring a future gate script; entry = commit (pre-commit lint runs Check 36); gain = an uncaught raw `br … --json` read whose br refusal decodes into 'no labels / no beads / nothing stale' inside a gate that stamps work across every consuming repo.
findings.fix: Scan the JOINED text, not per-line lines: strip backslash-newline continuations (`text.replace('\\\n', ' ')`) before matching, and harden the binary token to allow quotes around it (add `["']?\bbr\b["']?`). Add both evasion shapes as fixture cases in 36-br-envelope.test.sh so the sensor is mutation-tested against them.

findings.title: Check 35's origin rule silently skips records with no created_at and never scans in_progress beads — the backstop's live population is unsensed
findings.evidence: Probed live against the shipped check: a record with status open, created post-cutover, but NO created_at field produces `created = ""`, and `"" >= "2026-08-23"` is False — the origin rule never fires for it (verified: only the control bead was flagged). Likewise any record whose status is not exactly "open" is skipped at line 81, but this board's working state is `in_progress` (coordinator.sh selects in_progress claims as the live set) — an origin-less post-cutover bead sits in the committed board as in_progress for its entire working life and Check 35, the repair-window backstop its own docstring declares, reports the board clean the whole time. The check fails OPEN on a missing timestamp field and scopes away the in-flight population it exists to sense. Attack path: actor = any agent whose bead lost its origin: label (the exact failure this backstop was built to catch); entry = commit of .beads/issues.jsonl (the ledger commit is the gate per the check's design); gain = provenance axis unsensed for in-flight beads — origin-less work reaches refine with no red commit, defeating the origin axis the check claims to complete.
findings.fix: Treat an absent/unparseable created_at on an OPEN-row-shaped record as a violation (the field is mandatory in the derived board; a record that cannot prove its age must fail, not pass), and widen the status filter to the pre-close states the rule governs (`status in {"open", "in_progress"}`), keeping the never-scanned guarantee for closed beads. Add both rows to 35-board-integrity.test.sh.
